protocol.py: VERIFIED against plate map pcr-04. 18 of 18 wells hold what the plate map says.
  Destination: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 1). Reading of the request: 6 samples x
    3.

Labware for the technique (qPCR setup): 1 finding.
1. WARNING LABWARE-FOR-TECHNIQUE: The wrong kind of plate: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat is
  a flat plate, and qPCR setup needs a PCR plate or PCR strips
   line 38:  p20.dispense(8, target_well)
   The plate map says the technique is qPCR setup, which needs a PCR plate or PCR strips as
     its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 1,
     load name nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat), which is a flat plate. A thermocycler block is
     drilled for thin-walled 0.2 ml PCR wells; a flat plate does not fit in it, so the
     reaction can never be run. Every well still holds what the plate map asks for, so the
     map verifies; the plate is the problem.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2 and 10 more in slot 1.
   Fix: Load nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt (or the 200 ul PCR plate, or PCR strips
     on the aluminium block) as the destination; a flat plate cannot go in a thermocycler.
   Source: Opentrons, module setup: no error for an unusual labware and module combination
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/setup.html
   Source: Opentrons, thermocycler: takes the 200 ul full-skirt PCR plate
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/thermocycler.html
   Source: ABC-Bench (Liu et al. 2026): wrong labware identifiers, the commonest LLM error
           https://arxiv.org/html/2606.11150v1
   [924d4b10d970]

Where every liquid ended up (ul):
  liquid                             declared delivered in source elsewhere    lost
  master mix                            200.0     144.0      56.0       0.0     0.0
  sample 1                               30.0       6.0      24.0       0.0     0.0
  sample 2                               30.0       6.0      24.0       0.0     0.0
  sample 3                               30.0       6.0      24.0       0.0     0.0
  sample 4                               30.0       6.0      24.0       0.0     0.0
  sample 5                               30.0       6.0      24.0       0.0     0.0
  sample 6                               30.0       6.0      24.0       0.0     0.0

Prep sheet: what to put on the deck before the run.
  slot labware                               well  liquid                       load at least  declared
  3    Opentrons 24 Tube Rack with NEST 2 mL A1    master mix                           144.0     200.0
  4    Opentrons 96 Well Aluminum Block with A1    sample 1                               6.0      30.0
  4    Opentrons 96 Well Aluminum Block with A2    sample 2                               6.0      30.0
  4    Opentrons 96 Well Aluminum Block with A3    sample 3                               6.0      30.0
  4    Opentrons 96 Well Aluminum Block with A4    sample 4                               6.0      30.0
  4    Opentrons 96 Well Aluminum Block with A5    sample 5                               6.0      30.0
  4    Opentrons 96 Well Aluminum Block with A6    sample 6                               6.0      30.0
  Tips: 18 from Opentrons OT-2 96 Tip Rack 20 µL in slot 2.
  'Load at least' is what the robot draws. Add the dead volume of your tube or reservoir.

This checks the logic of the protocol: what goes where, and how much. It does not check the
  physics: whether a viscous liquid is pipetted accurately, or a drop stays on a tip.

labware.title: The wrong kind of plate: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat is a flat plate, and qPCR setup needs a PCR plate or PCR strips
labware.explanation: The plate map says the technique is qPCR setup, which needs a PCR plate or PCR strips as its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 1, load name nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat), which is a flat plate. A thermocycler block is drilled for thin-walled 0.2 ml PCR wells; a flat plate does not fit in it, so the reaction can never be run. Every well still holds what the plate map asks for, so the map verifies; the plate is the problem.
labware.fix: Load nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt (or the 200 ul PCR plate, or PCR strips on the aluminium block) as the destination; a flat plate cannot go in a thermocycler.

check_text:
protocol.py: 4 biology problems (2 warnings, 2 notes).

1. WARNING COLD-MODULE-NEVER-SET: A temperature module was loaded but never set
   line 43:  p20.aspirate(2, sample_source)
   At line 43 the robot draws from wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 4, on a
   temperature module that the protocol never sets. A temperature module stays at room
   temperature until `set_temperature` is called, so sample 1 (sample), sample 2 (sample),
   sample 3 (sample), sample 4 (sample) and 2 more sat on a block that was never cold; the
   robot pipetted there 18 times over the run. The person setting up the deck sees a module
   and assumes it is cold. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 4.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 4.
   Fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from Opentrons 96
   Well Aluminum Block with Generic PCR Strip 200 µL in slot 4, and
   `temp_module.deactivate()` at the end.
   Source: Opentrons, temperature module: at room temperature until set_temperature, which
   blocks
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/temperature_module.html
   Source: Thermo Fisher T4 ligase manual: keep on ice, use within minutes
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/t4dnaligase_1U_man.pdf
   Source: NEB: Q5 High-Fidelity PCR kit manual (add the polymerase last)
           https://www.neb.com/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale0555.pdf
   [cb33f0e026fe]

2. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 6 stocks
   line 43:  p20.aspirate(2, sample_source)
   At line 43 the tip went into sample 1 (well A1 in slot 4), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 4),
   sample 3 (well A3 in slot 4), sample 4 (well A4 in slot 4) and 2 more while it still
   carried master mix (tube A1 in slot 3) from an earlier step (this line did it 6 times). A
   tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so
   these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. The protocol drew from them
   again afterwards, but only into wells that were given that material on purpose anyway, so
   this run is not harmed. What is left in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A6 in slot 4.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 43 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [33e1f455bdcc]

3. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 18 wells of master mix with a sample
   line 38:  p20.dispense(8, target_well)
   At line 38 the robot starts putting master mix into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot
   1), and 18 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the
   mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated,
   or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate
   can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2 and 10 more in
   slot 1.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2 and 10 more in slot 1.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 8 ul of master mix and 2 ul of water in place of
   the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [482a6b0130e5]

4. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 18 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4
and 2 more went in (20% of the well)
   line 44:  p20.dispense(2, target_well)
   At line 44 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 2 more to wells A1,
   A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2 and 10 more in slot 1, which already held master mix (this
   line did it 18 times). The addition was 20% of the well, nothing mixed the well
   afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do
   not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated.
   A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be,
   mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2 and 10 more in slot 1.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2 and 10 more in slot 1 after line 44:
   `mix_after=(5, 8)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 8, well)`, with the volume about
   80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [36cae40cf1b8]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

No well on this plate holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate can tell that from a real one.
